a: one; used before a word for one person or thing (a day, a job)
about: on the subject of; also: almost (about 10 minutes)
adel: a man's name (Omar's family name in the story)
ago: before now (two years ago = two years before today)
an: one; used instead of 'a' before a vowel sound (an answer)
and: a word that joins two things together
angry: feeling very upset because something is bad or unfair
answer: what you say or write when someone asks you something
ask: say something to get an answer from someone
at: in or near a place or time (at home, at 5 o'clock)
bank: a place that keeps people's money safe
be: a very common verb: am, is, are, was, were (I am happy)
big: large; also: very important (a big day)
bored: not interested; tired of doing nothing new
but: a word that shows something different or opposite
call: phone someone; a call center is an office where people answer phone calls
celebrate: do something fun because of a happy day
center: the middle; also: a place for a special activity (a call center)
ceremony: a big, special event with many people
certificate: an official paper that shows you finished your studies
clap: hit your hands together to make a noise, to show you like something
company: a business; a group of people who work together to make money
congratulations: something you say to someone when they do something great
day: 24 hours; the time when it is light
degree: what you get when you finish university
do: a common verb for actions (do homework); also used in questions (Do you…?)
eat: put food in your mouth and swallow it
english: the language of the UK, the USA and many other countries
example: one thing that shows what others are like
excited: very happy and full of energy about something good
eye: the part of your face you see with
family: a mother, a father and their children
father: a man who has a child; dad
feel: have a feeling, like happy, sad or nervous
for: used to show who gets something or why (a gift for you)
fresh: new; just made or just finished (a fresh graduate)
friend: a person you know well and like
future: the time that comes after now
go: move from one place to another
good: nice, right or of high quality
graduate: a person who finished university; also: finish university
graduation: the day you finish university and get your certificate
hard: difficult; also: with a lot of effort (hard work)
have: own or hold something; also used to make other verb forms
he: a man or boy (that we talked about before)
her: belonging to a woman or girl; also: a woman or girl (I see her)
his: belonging to a man or boy
i: the word you use for yourself
important: having a big effect; it matters a lot
it: a thing or animal (that we talked about before)
job: work that you do to get money
journey: a long trip; also: the way from where you are to where you want to be
karim: a man's name (Omar's best friend in the story)
kitchen: the room where you cook food
laptop: a small computer that you can carry
late: after the usual or right time
laugh: make a happy sound when something is funny
life: the time a person is alive; how you live
little: small; also: not much (a little nervous)
look: turn your eyes to see something
mirror: a glass that shows you your face
mother: a woman who has a child; mom
name: the word people call you
nervous: a little afraid before something important
new: not old; just made or just bought
next: the one that comes after this one
night: the dark time when people sleep
noon: 12 o'clock in the middle of the day
omar: a man's name (the main character of the story)
on: touching the top of something; also: wearing (puts on a suit)
one: the number 1; also: a single person or thing
photo: a picture you take with a camera or phone
proud: very happy because of something good you or someone did
put: move something to a place; put on = wear clothes
question: something you ask to get an answer
remember: keep something in your mind; not forget
restaurant: a place where you pay to eat a meal
see: use your eyes to notice something
she: a woman or girl (that we talked about before)
sleep: rest at night with your eyes closed
smile: make a happy face with your mouth
so: very; also: for that reason; also used to start a question (So, what's next?)
son: a boy or man who is someone's child
stage: the high place in a hall where people speak or perform
stand: be on your feet; stand up = get up from a chair
student: a person who studies at a school or university
suit: a jacket and trousers made from the same cloth
take: get something with your hands; take photos = make pictures
tears: water that comes from your eyes when you cry
that: the one over there; also used to join ideas
the: used before a thing we already know about
there: in that place; there are = some things exist
they: the people or things we talked about
think: use your mind; have an idea
to: toward a place; also used before a verb (to eat)
university: a place where people study after school to get a degree
up: toward a higher place; wake up = stop sleeping
work: do a job; also: the job you do
yes: a word that means you agree; the opposite of no
you: the person I am talking to
